definitions.explanation: Shoes specifically worn outdoors, in contrast to {内履|うちば}き (indoor shoes). Common in schools, hospitals, and other places where indoor and outdoor footwear are separated.

examples.japanese: {外履|そとば}きはここで{脱|ぬ}いでください。
examples.english: Please take off your outdoor shoes here.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}では{外履|そとば}きと{内履|うちば}きを{分|わ}けている。
examples.english: At school, outdoor and indoor shoes are kept separate.

examples.japanese: {病院|びょういん}に{入|はい}る{前|まえ}に{外履|そとば}きを{袋|ふくろ}に{入|い}れて{持|も}ち{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: Before entering the hospital I put my outdoor shoes in a bag and carried them with me.

notes:
Compound of {外|そと} (outside) + {履|は}く (to wear on the feet). The institutional practice of switching shoes is widespread in Japan: schools, gyms, hospitals, and some workplaces require {内履|うちば}き indoors.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外履|そとば}きを{脱|ぬ}ぐ: to take off outdoor shoes
- {外履|そとば}き{用|よう}: for outdoor use
- {外履|そとば}き{入|い}れ: bag/locker for outdoor shoes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {内履|うちば}き: indoor shoes (antonym)
- {上履|うわば}き: indoor school shoes — specifically the soft shoes worn at school
- {下駄箱|げたばこ}: shoe cupboard at an entryway
